formats.name: List / Roundup
formats.purpose: Give several useful items without overcrowding any slide.
generationRules: Use exactly six concise items across the three middle slides.
Each item must be useful and grounded in the supplied business context.

slides.instruction: Introduce the useful list and why it matters.
Present items one and two as two short list items.
Present items three and four as two short list items.
Present items five and six as two short list items.
State the practical takeaway and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Mistakes
formats.purpose: Show three recognizable mistakes and what to do instead.
generationRules: Use exactly three mistakes.
Do not blame or shame the audience.

slides.instruction: Introduce the three mistakes and their consequence.
Explain the first specific mistake.
Explain the second distinct mistake.
Explain the third distinct mistake.
Explain what to do instead and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: How-To / Steps
formats.purpose: Teach a useful result through three ordered steps.
generationRules: The three steps must be ordered and actionable.
Do not skip the connection between steps.

slides.instruction: Promise a supported result or introduce the process.
Give the first actionable step.
Give the second actionable step.
Give the third actionable step.
State the useful result and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Comparison
formats.purpose: Compare two meaningful choices and explain the important difference.
generationRules: Compare choices with a real difference.
Do not invent numerical values or force an artificial winner.

slides.instruction: Introduce the two choices and the decision that matters.
Explain option A fairly.
Explain option B fairly.
Explain the most useful difference between the options.
Give a conditional recommendation or takeaway and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Swap / Do This Instead
formats.purpose: Offer three simple replacements for a weaker habit or choice.
generationRules: Every replacement must be practical.
Do not imply that one choice is universally correct.

slides.instruction: Introduce the benefit of making these swaps.
Give the first replacement and why it helps.
Give the second replacement and why it helps.
Give the third replacement and why it helps.
Summarize how to choose a useful swap and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Myth vs Fact
formats.purpose: Correct three common misunderstandings with careful explanations.
generationRules: Use exactly three myths.
Correct only claims supported by the supplied context or safe general knowledge without precise invented numbers.

slides.instruction: Introduce the misconception worth correcting.
State the first myth and its correction.
State the second myth and its correction.
State the third myth and its correction.
State the careful takeaway and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Cheat Sheet
formats.purpose: Create a compact reference people can save and revisit.
generationRules: Keep every reference item concise.
Prefer scannable list modes on the middle slides.

slides.instruction: Name the reference and its practical use.
Give the first reference section as two or three short items.
Give the second reference section as two or three short items.
Give the third reference section as two or three short items.
Explain how to use the reference and add a save CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Checklist
formats.purpose: Help the audience check six important things before acting.
generationRules: Use exactly six checks across the three middle slides.
Each check must be short and testable.

slides.instruction: Explain what the checklist helps the reader verify.
Present checks one and two.
Present checks three and four.
Present checks five and six.
State the final reminder and add a save CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Framework / Formula
generationRules: The three parts must form one coherent system.
Do not invent a branded framework name that implies external authority.

slides.instruction: Introduce the framework and the problem it organizes.
Explain the first part.
Explain the second part.
Explain the third part.
Explain how the three parts work together and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Breakdown / Anatomy
formats.purpose: Explain three components of an idea or process.
generationRules: Each component must be distinct.
The final slide must explain what the breakdown means in practice.

slides.instruction: Introduce what is being broken down and why it matters.
Explain the first component.
Explain the second component.
Explain the third component.
Explain the practical meaning and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Problem to Cause to Solution
formats.purpose: Explain one recognizable problem, its cause, and what to change.
generationRules: Keep the story focused on one problem.
The solution must address the stated cause.

slides.instruction: State the recognizable problem as the hook.
Explain why the problem happens.
Clarify the most important cause or consequence.
Explain the supported change or mechanism.
State the next action or takeaway and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Beginner Roadmap
formats.purpose: Show a beginner the correct order for getting started.
generationRules: Use beginner-friendly language.
The order must be meaningful rather than arbitrary.

slides.instruction: Address the beginner and name the useful outcome.
Explain the first thing to focus on.
Explain the next step.
Explain the third step.
Explain what to focus on going forward and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Resource Collection
formats.purpose: Give six useful resources, tools, foods, exercises, templates, or references.
generationRules: Use exactly six resources across the middle slides.
Do not invent current product features, rankings, links, or numerical claims.

slides.instruction: Introduce the collection and its practical use.
Present resources one and two.
Present resources three and four.
Present resources five and six.
Explain how to use the collection and add a save CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Examples / Inspiration
formats.purpose: Teach through three concrete examples and the pattern connecting them.
generationRules: Use exactly three examples.
Do not present invented brands or customers as real evidence.

slides.instruction: Introduce what the examples help the reader understand.
Give the first concrete example.
Give the second concrete example.
Give the third concrete example.
Explain the pattern connecting the examples and add a soft CTA only when useful.

formats.name: Before to After / Transformation
formats.purpose: Show the improvement created by one meaningful change.
generationRules: The transformation may be conceptual rather than physical.
Do not guarantee results or invent unsupported before-and-after metrics.

slides.instruction: Introduce the meaningful transformation.
Describe the original situation.
Explain the one meaningful change.
Describe the supported improvement without guaranteeing results.
State the lesson and add a soft CTA only when useful.
